rounds.text: Bajaj Auto Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 16,049 per share against a market price of Rs 11,460, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 28.6% [E46, E47]. The company’s fundamental profitability is elite, demonstrated by a stellar return on equity of 27.67% and a return on capital employed of 24.52%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 11.38% and 12.47% respectively [E9, E10]. Sales and profit momentum are explosive, highlighted by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 37% and compounded profit growth of 55% [E17, E21], accompanied by a rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 [E64]. Furthermore, management’s commitment to shareholder returns was definitively proven by a board-approved payout of 100% of last year's profits via a final dividend and a tender-route buyback at Rs 12,000 per share [E94], alongside massive surplus cash in excess of Rs 21,000 crores [E93]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is elevated at 8.25x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.91x [E7], and cash conversion for Mar 2026 sits low at 0.25x due to profits outpacing operating cash flow [E34].

Bajaj Auto carries a rich valuation that is heavily extended beyond sector benchmarks, trading at a price-to-book multiple of 8.25x against a sector benchmark of just 2.91x [E2, E7]. This expensive pricing is further exacerbated by negative institutional money flows and a meaningful drop in foreign institutional ownership from 14.37% down to 9.01% [E43, E45]. Fundamental execution also displays glaring disconnects, notably evidenced by a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.25x where reported profits vastly outpace operating cash flows [E34]. Operating margins are stagnant at 20% with an inconsistent trend over the last two years, signalling that profitability is failing to expand despite the lofty multiple [E30, E32]. Conceded: the company boasts a robust ROE of 27.67% and a strong trailing twelve-month profit growth of 55% [E9, E21]. However, this growth faces headwinds from management's own admissions that supply chain disruptions, logistics issues, and ransomware attacks have impaired product availability by 10% to 15% [E96].

Conceded: price-to-book sits at 8.25x against a sector benchmark of 2.91x [E2, E7]. However, this premium valuation is fully justified by elite operational returns, including an ROA of 14.96% versus a sector benchmark of 6.04% and an ROE of 27.67% compared to 11.38% [E8, E9]. While foreign institutional ownership changed, domestic institutions expanded their stake from 9.03% to 13.42%, proving strong local conviction [E43, E44]. On cash conversion, trailing numbers tell a different story: operating cash flow reached Rs 2,597 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 1,885 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the stagnant operating margin argument ignores the impressive 55% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and 21% over 3 years [E21, E20]. Finally, the operational headwinds from supply chain issues are being aggressively countered by a planned 25% capacity expansion up to 9 million units per annum and robust export momentum [E84, E80].

The bull’s reliance on high ROE and ROA [E8, E9] ignores the reality that the stock is trading at a significant premium to its sector, with a P/B of 8.14x versus a benchmark of 2.91x [E7]. While the bull highlights domestic institutional buying, it glosses over the fact that foreign institutional holdings have dropped by 5.36 percentage points [E43], resulting in an overall negative money flow signal [E45]. The claim that cash conversion is strong is directly contradicted by the Mar 2026 data, which shows operating cash flow was only 46% of operating profit [E37] and a concerning cash conversion ratio of 0.25x [E34]. Conceded: the company generated Rs 2,597 Cr in operating cash flow [E35]. However, the bull’s focus on profit growth fails to address that operating margins have remained stagnant at 20% over the last three years [E30]. Furthermore, the aggressive capacity expansion [E84] must be viewed alongside the fact that borrowings have surged from Rs 9,364 Cr to Rs 22,713 Cr in just one year [E40], adding significant leverage to the balance sheet [E38].

Conceded: [E7] shows a P/B of 8.14x against the sector benchmark of 2.91x, but this rich multiple is fully justified by elite returns on capital that tower over the same sector [E8, E9, E10]. While foreign institutions reduced stakes [E43], domestic institutions aggressively stepped up their ownership by 4.39 percentage points [E44], reflecting strong local conviction in the underlying business. Conceded: [E34] and [E37] highlight a lower cash conversion ratio and operating cash flow percentage for March 2026, yet the company still delivered absolute operating cash flow of Rs 2,597 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 1,885 Cr [E35, E36]. Stagnant operating margins at 20% [E30] matter far less when compounded sales and profit growth are accelerating at 20% and 21% over 3 years, culminating in a stellar 55% profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E16, E20, E21]. Finally, the surge in borrowings to fund a 25% capacity expansion toward 9 million units [E40, E84] represents an aggressive, growth-focused deployment of capital backed by surplus cash in excess of ₹21,000 crores [E93], rather than distress leverage.

The bull justifies a P/B of 8.14x [E7] by citing high returns, yet this ignores that the stock is trading at a significant premium to its sector benchmark [E6, E7] while institutional money flow remains negative [E45, E70]. While domestic institutions increased their stake [E44], this does not negate the fact that foreign institutional holdings have dropped by 5.36 percentage points [E43], signaling a broader retreat from the stock. Conceded: the company generated Rs 2,597 Cr in operating cash flow [E35], but the bull glosses over the fact that this represents only 46% of operating profit [E37], indicating a concerning disconnect between reported earnings and actual cash generation [E34]. The bull frames the surge in borrowings to Rs 22,713 Cr [E40] as growth-focused, yet this represents a massive increase from Rs 9,364 Cr a year earlier, adding significant leverage to the balance sheet [E40]. Furthermore, the bull highlights accelerating growth [E16, E20, E21] while ignoring that management itself expects a slowdown in the motorcycle category to 7% to 9% in the near term [E78]. Finally, the bull ignores that operating margins have remained stagnant at 20% for three years [E30], suggesting that the recent profit growth may be difficult to sustain as the company faces supply chain disruptions and inflationary pressures [E96, E97, E98].

Management estimates the near-term motorcycle category growth to slow down to 7% to 9%.
evidence.quote: This is bound to slow down the motorcycle category from its rocking 20% growth in Q4 to we estimate 7% to 9% in the near term.

evidence.fact: Management expects the motorcycle industry to continue to grow at 12% to 15%.
evidence.quote: We expect this growth momentum in the industry to continue and the motorcycle industry to continue to grow at, say, 12% to 15%.

evidence.fact: The export business is on track to deliver its highest-ever top-line performance in USD terms this financial year.
evidence.quote: In fact, the business is on the path to deliver its highest ever top line performance in USD terms this financial year.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the demand environment across both domestic and international key markets is very positive.
evidence.quote: Having said that, the demand environment, both in domestic and international, particularly in our key markets, is very positive, though the business environment may still be a bit volatile.

evidence.fact: The demand environment softened in April due to general inflation, increased vehicle prices, LPG shortages, and manpower migration.
evidence.quote: The demand environment, it has softened in April due to general inflation, increased prices of our vehicles, LPG shortages, manpower migration and the LPG shortage-led effect on the consumer sentiment.

evidence.fact: The top 30 overseas markets grew by about 10% in the quarter, with Bajaj Auto sales growing at 15%.
evidence.quote: The top 30 overseas markets collectively accounting for nearly 75% of the emerging market, industry grew by about 10% in this quarter with our sales growing at 15%, thereby signalling an increase of market share in these key markets.

evidence.fact: The company is undertaking a capacity expansion of nearly 25% from the current 7 million units per annum to progressively go up to 9 million units per annum.
evidence.quote: So, with an eye on the future, we are undertaking an expansion of capacity by almost 25% from the current 7 million units per annum across different businesses to progressively go up to 9 million units per annum.

evidence.fact: Capex for the year was approximately INR500 crores, split equally between ICE and EV investments.
evidence.quote: Capex for the year was approximately INR500 crores, split equally between ICE and EV investments.

evidence.fact: Joint KTM-Triumph showrooms are planned to expand from about 50 operational outlets to over 100 by March.
evidence.quote: We currently have about 50 KT showrooms operational and plan to expand these to over 100 by March.

evidence.fact: Commodity inflation intensified during the quarter, taking the overall impact to about 4.5% of revenue.
evidence.quote: Inflation across the metals complex accelerated meaningfully through May, taking the overall inflationary impact for the quarter to about 4.5% of revenue.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margins for the quarter reached 20.9%, an improvement of 10 basis points sequentially.
evidence.quote: EBITDA margins inched up to 20.9%, an improvement of 10 basis points sequentially despite the hyperinflationary commodity environment that I'd spoken about.

evidence.fact: Quarter 4 EBITDA margins held steady at 20.8%.
evidence.quote: EBITDA came in at INR3,323 crores and the margins at 20.8% sustained despite challenges in the operating environment.

evidence.fact: Chetak manufacturing capacity has now reached 50,000 units per month.
evidence.quote: And we have now a capacity of 50,000 units per month.

evidence.fact: Exports crossed the 600,000 units mark after 15 quarters.
evidence.quote: The BU crossed the 200,000 average per month sales level in October '25 after nearly 40 months and maintained this level through the remainder of the quarter, surpassing the 600,000 units mark after 15 quarters.

evidence.fact: The Pro-Biking business delivered a combined volume of over 35,000 units, registering growth of around 50% year-on-year.
evidence.quote: The 2 brands together delivered a record domestic performance with combined volumes of over 35,000 units, registering robust growth of around 50% year-on-year and marking the highest-ever quarterly performance for the business, lifted also by the positive sentiment.

evidence.fact: Surplus cash stood in excess of INR21,000 crores at the end of the June quarter.
evidence.quote: The balance sheet continues to remain very healthy with surplus cash in excess of INR21,000 crores at the end of the June quarter, well managed and providing sufficient fuel for future growth investments, strategic opportunities and improved shareholder returns.

evidence.fact: The Board approved a payout of 100% of profits made last year via a final dividend and a tender-route buyback.
evidence.quote: Lastly, the Board of Directors at its meeting earlier today approved a payout of 100% of the profits that we have made last year in recognition of the 100 years milestone of the Bajaj family in India and with Bajaj Auto being the flagship company that started it all. his will be split as follows a final dividend of INR150 per share that will aggregate to INR4,192 crores and the balance of about INR5,633 crores will be towards a buyback under the tender route at a buyback price of INR12,000 per share.

evidence.fact: Surplus cash closed at about INR 15,000 crores.
evidence.quote: We continue to deliver strong and consistent cash generation, closing the quarter with surplus cash of about INR15,000 crores.

evidence.fact: Management noted that supply chain disruptions, logistics issues, and a ransomware attack impaired availabilities by about 10% to 15%.
evidence.quote: All of these above issues combined impaired availabilities by about 10% to 15%, more so in exports, high-end bikes and EVs.

evidence.fact: Supply chain difficulties in terms of LPG shortages, manpower availability, and outbound logistics have impaired availability to service demand by about 10% to 15%.
evidence.quote: Supply chain difficulties in terms of the LPG shortage, manpower availability and outbound logistics to overseas markets have impaired availability to service demand by about 10% to 15%.

evidence.fact: Noble metals including platinum, palladium, and rhodium saw sharp increases, while aluminium, copper, nickel, and lead also continued to harden.
evidence.quote: Noble Metals especially platinum, palladium and rhodium all saw sharp increases, whilst aluminium, copper, nickel and lead also continued to harden.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: The company aims to accomplish an exhaustive portfolio makeover for domestic motorcycles within the next 6 weeks.
evidence.quote: Our aim is to accomplish this exhaustive portfolio makeover within the next 6 weeks.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: Management intends to move BMAG and KTM AG to quarterly reporting as a voluntary action to align with Bajaj Auto's reporting calendar.
evidence.quote: Going forward, it is our intention to move BMAG, KTM AG to quarterly reporting as a voluntary action to align with Bajaj Auto's reporting calendar and as a measure of good governance and transparency.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 4 months): Over 8 more interventions in the Pulsar portfolio will be made in the next 4 months.
evidence.quote: The waves of these interventions will be unrelenting here onwards with over 8 more such interventions being made in the next 4 months.
